title: Renewal Interview-Led Postmortem Canvas
content:
Purpose:
This working canvas is designed to drive interviewer-led renewal postmortems that are evidence-first, action-oriented, and easily converted into QBR inputs and a prioritized winback plan. Use when a renewal is lost or downgraded, when a customer signals intent to churn, or for recurring recurring-risk accounts flagged by renewal health scoring.

When to use (quick):
- Lost renewal detected within renewal window or immediately post-contract end.
- High ARR accounts with ambiguous reasons for non-renewal.
- Pattern detection: same failure mode across >3 accounts in 90 days.

One‑line summary (template):
- Customer: [Company X] | ARR bucket: [>$250k] | Renewal outcome: [Declined] | Primary driver: [Procurement & compliance timing] | Impact: [Immediate revenue loss + 3m ramp to re-engage]

Postmortem objectives:
1) Reconstruct a minimal factual timeline (dates, decisions, stakeholders).
2) Surface the 1–3 root causes with supporting evidence.
3) Generate counterfactual scenarios (what could we have changed).
4) Produce a prioritized 30/60/90 day recovery & prevent plan for CS + Product + Sales.

Root Cause Canvas (fill for each hypothesis)
- Hypothesis label: (concise)
- Observable evidence: (tickets, usage, emails, contract notes, exec asks, SSO logs)
- Impact on renewal decision: (yes/no/partial + why)
- Likelihood: (low/med/high)
- Actionable fix: (immediate step + medium-term change)
- Owner & ETA: (name + date)

Timeline Reconstruction Guidance
- Minimum timeline rows: First engagement date, Onboard complete, First value milestone, Pre-renewal check-in dates, Renewal notice sent, Renewal decision date.
- Sources: account repo, deal notes, shared drive attachments, Calendars, support ticket system, audit logs.
- Anchor each event to a primary artifact (link or ticket id).

Interview Guide (roles + sample questions)
- Exec sponsor (CEO/CPO/CIO):
  - Was the value proposition still top priority at renewal? If not, what shifted?
  - Were there external constraints (budget freeze, org restructure, new vendor mandate)?
  - Did you expect Redwood to discuss alternatives (on-prem, dedicated capacity)?
- Technical owner/architect: 
  - What were the top blockers in the last 90 days (integration, performance, security)?
  - Were there unresolved acceptance criteria for the project?
  - Were there compliance artifacts we didn’t supply or timelines we missed?
- Procurement/legal: 
  - What were the gating items for approval?
  - Was pricing the primary blocker or was contract language/SLAs?
- End users/admins: 
  - Did the product meet day-to-day needs? Examples of where it did/didn’t.

Data & Evidence Checklist
- Usage metrics: active seats, API calls/day, tokens/day, tail-latency percentiles.
- Health signals: error spike dates, support ticket counts, open critical bugs.
- Sales notes: discounted offers, negotiation artefacts, signed amendments.
- Security/compliance: pending assessments, ATO timelines, certification gaps.
- Communication record: last 6 months of key emails/meeting notes.

Renewal Decision Scoring (quick rubric)
- Score 0–5 on: Business alignment, Product fit, Operational reliability, Procurement friction, Commercial terms.
- Aggregate: >=20 strong retention, 12–19 uncertain, <12 high risk.

Counterfactual Scenarios (examples to build for QBR)
- Scenario A (Fast path): If we had delivered security attestation before vendor list freeze, customer would likely have renewed. Required: priority product sprint + tailored attestation.
- Scenario B (Commercial path): If Sales had offered a short bridge commitment (3 months at reduced rate) tied to feature delivery, renewal could have been deferred rather than lost.
- Scenario C (Fallback path): If automatic fallback to a lower-cost compatible model was available, cost objections might have been reduced.

30/60/90 Winback & Prevent Plan Template
- 0–30 days (triage): assign owner, schedule executive readout, deliver immediate artifact (security packet / pilot credits), open PR for critical bug, set measurement SLA.
- 30–60 days (remediation): complete promised deliverables, pilot with one team, negotiate bridge/commercial terms if needed.
- 60–90 days (conversion): exec-level review + final contract negotiation, incorporate product/process changes into roadmap.

Internal Communication Templates (short)
- Slack to CS leadership: "Lost renewal: [Company]. Primary hypothesis: [X]. Immediate owner: [name]. Exec readout scheduled: [date]. Key ask: [security packet]."
- Jira ticket title: "POSTMORTEM: Renewal lost — [Company] — primary hypothesis [X]"

Example mini-case (fictional, filled quickly)
- Customer: BrightLeaf Analytics | ARR: $320k | Outcome: Declined renewal
- Primary driver(s): sudden security policy update requiring on-prem deployment; Redwood Private not yet certified for their processor profile + procurement window closed.
- Timeline highlights: policy issued 2024-11-02, BrightLeaf request for on-prem estimate 2024-11-06, Redwood response lacking certification evidence 2024-11-09, renewal notice 2024-12-01, decision 2024-12-12.
- Root cause hypothesis: Product readiness/certification gap (high likelihood). Evidence: support ticket, executive ask emails, procurement rejection note.
- Counterfactual: If we had previously prioritized the certification or provided a documented mitigation (signed interim security attestation + roadmap commitment), BrightLeaf would likely have accepted a 3mo bridge.
- 0–30 owner actions: CS lead to secure interim attestation (Owner: Priya Khatri, ETA: 2025-03-10).

Ownership & Follow-up (required fields)
- Postmortem owner: (name)
- Exec sponsor follow-up: (name)
- Product changes PR: (link/jira)
- Customer communication date: (YYYY-MM-DD)

Deliverables for QBR and GTM
- One-slide summary for QBR (summary template provided above).
- Winback playbook w/ measurable KPIs (re-engagement rate, time-to-contract).
- Prevent list: prioritized product gaps, certification roadmap, CS process fixes.

Appendix: common loss archetypes (short)
- Compliance/Regulatory timing mismatch
- Procurement cost-savings mandate
- Value not realized (lack of measurable outcomes)
- Competing product bundling (vendor consolidation)
- Multi-stakeholder misalignment (no executive champion)

How to close the loop
- Add final postmortem to Confluence, tag product & sales leads, schedule a 30-minute cross-functional readout.
- Track the 30/60/90 plan in Jira and link progress to the original postmortem ticket.
- Add the case to renewal analytics cohort for pattern detection (monthly review).

Notes to the interviewer (meta):
- Don’t lead witnesses: phrase questions to elicit facts and artifacts.
- Prioritize exec & procurement interviews early — they reveal immovable constraints.
- Rate hypotheses by both impact and feasibility to change.

End of canvas. Use this as a living template; add QBR-ready slides and an anonymized case library when finalizing.
